topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: A channel that uses only one intermediary between the producer and the consumer (e.g. producer to retailer to consumer) is called a:
e: The number of levels equals the number of intermediaries. One retailer between producer and consumer makes a one-level channel.

topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: General insurance business in India was nationalised in 1972, after which distribution was handled by:
o: The four subsidiaries of GIC and their development officers and agents
e: After 1972, National, New India, Oriental and United India (under GIC) wrote general business through their own branches, development officers and agents until liberalisation.

topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: The evolution of insurance distribution in India after 2000 is best described as a move from:
o: A single tied-agency channel to multiple regulated channels (corporate agents, brokers, aggregators, IMFs, POSPs, online)
e: Liberalisation and successive IRDAI regulations created a diversified distribution architecture to match different customer segments and products.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: Which of the following is NOT a type of channel conflict?
e: Channel conflict is classified as vertical (between levels), horizontal (same level) and multi-channel (between different channel types). Solvency is a regulatory capital concept.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: An insurer's agency channel has fixed annual cost of ₹30 crore (branches, managers) and variable cost of 10% of premium; a corporate-agent channel has negligible fixed cost but 25% variable cost. At what annual premium are the two channels equal in cost?
e: Equate costs: 30 + 0.10P = 0.25P, so 0.15P = 30 and P = ₹200 crore. Above ₹200 crore the agency channel is cheaper; below it, the corporate agent channel is.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: Which approach to channel conflict is 'co-optation'?
o: Winning the support of channel members by including their leaders in advisory councils or boards
e: Co-optation gives intermediaries a voice in governance to align them with the producer's goals; mediation and arbitration are third-party methods.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The minimum age for appointment as an individual insurance agent in India is:
e: Applicants must be at least 18 years old, have passed 10th standard and cleared the prescribed examination.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: An insurer's data shows that 20% of its agents bring in 80% of its premium. This observation is an application of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 80/20 (Pareto) rule suggests concentrating management attention and support on the vital few high-performing agents and the most valuable customers.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following persons is disqualified from being appointed as an insurance agent under Section 42(3) of the Insurance Act, 1938?
o: A person with a graduate degree
A person found guilty of criminal misappropriation, breach of trust, cheating or forgery
e: Disqualifications include minority, unsound mind, conviction for specified offences, and failure to pass the examination; age above 18 and gender are not bars.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The registration fee payable by a corporate agent to IRDAI is:
e: Corporate agents pay ₹10,000 (plus taxes) on registration and ₹25,000 (plus taxes) on renewal; IMFs pay ₹5,000 and ₹2,000 respectively.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A reinsurance broker must maintain a minimum net worth of:
e: Reinsurance and composite brokers must keep net worth of 50% of minimum capital (₹2 crore and ₹2.5 crore); direct brokers must keep ₹50 lakh.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A broker whose annual remuneration including rewards exceeds ₹5 crore must appoint a:
e: The Brokers Regulations, 2018 require a dedicated compliance officer for brokers earning above ₹5 crore in a financial year.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which statement about bancassurance in India is INCORRECT?
o: Banks may now tie up with up to nine insurers in each category
A bank selling insurance underwrites the risk on its own balance sheet
Banks must obtain IRDAI registration as corporate agents to sell insurance
Banks distribute insurance as corporate agents under IRDAI regulations
e: The bank only distributes; the insurer underwrites and bears the risk. Banks need corporate agent registration and may tie up with up to nine insurers per category.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The risk of 'coercive selling' in bancassurance refers to:
o: Insurers coercing banks to sign agreements
Customers forcing banks to sell insurance
Bank staff linking loans or other banking services to the purchase of an insurance policy
e: Tying insurance to loan sanction is a well-known mis-selling concern; regulators have cautioned banks against making insurance a condition for banking services.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A web aggregator's registration with IRDAI is valid for:
e: Like other intermediaries, web aggregators are registered for three years, with renewal fee ₹25,000 plus taxes.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The Principal Officer of an Insurance Marketing Firm must have at least:
e: The IMF Principal Officer must be a graduate and pass the prescribed training and examination; Insurance Sales Persons need 12th standard.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following is a MERIT of the POSP channel for insurers?
o: It provides a low-cost, scalable field force for simple products with quick onboarding
It is exempt from all IRDAI oversight
It can be used for reinsurance
It allows sale of complex products with high underwriting
e: POSPs can be onboarded quickly after 15 hours of training and an in-house exam, enabling reach for standardised products at low cost.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Under the POS-Life product norms, a non-linked non-participating endowment sold by a POSP must have:
o: A term of at least 25 years
A sum assured of at least ₹1 crore
A term between 5 and 20 years and maximum sum assured of ₹10 lakh (excluding accidental death benefit)
e: POS endowment products are capped at ₹10 lakh sum assured with 5–20 year terms and non-medical underwriting to keep them simple.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A key MERIT of the broker channel for a corporate customer is that the broker:
o: Provides independent advice, risk assessment and negotiates terms with several insurers on the client's behalf
Sets the premium rates for the market
e: Brokers represent the client; for large commercial risks they analyse exposures, design programmes and obtain competitive quotes, including from reinsurance markets.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: An insurer sells the same term plan through its website at a premium 10% lower than through agents. Agents complain that customers meet them for advice and then buy online. This is an example of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Conflict between different channel types serving the same market (agents versus the insurer's own online channel) is multi-channel conflict; horizontal conflict would be between two agents.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: Which of the following is NOT one of the service-output demands that distribution should satisfy?
e: Customers want convenience, variety, short waiting time, suitable lot size and after-sales support; investment yield is an insurer-level metric.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: The SERVQUAL dimension 'empathy' refers to:
o: Caring, individualised attention given to customers
e: Empathy is understanding and attending to individual customer needs; tangibles cover appearance, reliability covers accuracy and responsiveness covers speed.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: In the gaps model, the 'knowledge gap' arises when:
o: Staff fail to deliver to standards
Management does not accurately understand what customers expect
e: The knowledge gap is between customer expectations and management's perception of them; it is closed through research and feedback from frontline distributors.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: A customer values 'convenience' highly and 'advice' little. The channel that creates the most value for this customer when buying motor insurance is likely to be:
o: A home visit by an agent
Instant online renewal through an app
A seminar at a bank branch
e: Value depends on the customer's service-output priorities; for a standard motor renewal, speed and ease dominate, so a digital self-service channel fits best.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: 'Customer delight' goes beyond satisfaction because it:
o: Occurs when performance exceeds expectations, creating emotional attachment and advocacy
Occurs when performance merely meets expectations
Is measured by the claims ratio
e: Satisfaction is meeting expectations; delight is exceeding them. Distributors create delight through proactive service, e.g. assisting with a claim beyond the call of duty.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Perishability' of a service, applied to insurance distribution, implies that:
o: Selling capacity (agent time, counter time) that is unused cannot be stored, so productivity management is critical
Insurance is sold only in seasons
e: Service capacity cannot be inventoried; an unproductive agent-day is lost for ever, which is why activity management and lead flow matter.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Which statement about India's insurance market is CORRECT (as per recent IRDAI annual reports)?
o: India's insurance penetration is roughly 3.7–4% of GDP, below the global average, indicating large untapped potential
Non-life penetration in India exceeds life penetration
India's insurance penetration is above the world average
Insurance density in India exceeds US$1,000
e: Overall penetration is around 3.7% (life about 2.8%, non-life about 1%), below the world average of about 7%, and density is around US$90–95 — the core distribution opportunity.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: A general insurer finds that its agency channel brings in motor business at an acquisition cost of 18% of premium, while its direct website brings it at 6%. The insurer should most appropriately:
o: Raise agency commission to match the website cost
Compare the channels on persistency, claims quality, volume and customer segment before changing the mix
Ignore the data because channel cost is irrelevant to strategy
Close the agency channel immediately because it costs more
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Channel mix decisions weigh cost against reach, volume, business quality and customer preference. Acquisition cost alone does not justify eliminating a channel that may serve segments the website cannot.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: A regular-premium life policy has annual premium ₹40,000; the insurer's first-year acquisition cost (commission, medicals, issuance) is ₹22,000 and the annual contribution available to recover it is ₹6,000. Ignoring interest, in which policy year does the insurer break even on this policy?
e: Shortfall after year 1 = ₹22,000 − ₹6,000 = ₹16,000; recovered at ₹6,000 a year it needs about 2.67 more years, so break-even falls in year 4. Early lapses therefore cause losses.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Orphan policies' are:
o: Policies taken on the lives of orphans
Policies whose servicing agent has left the insurer, leaving the policyholder without an assigned advisor
e: Agent attrition creates orphan policies that suffer poor servicing and persistency; insurers reassign them to other agents or branch servicing teams.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Which of the following represents an OPPORTUNITY for insurance distribution arising from demographic change in India?
o: Growing young, urban, salaried population with rising disposable income and digital familiarity
e: India's demographic dividend and rising incomes expand the market for protection, health and savings products, especially through digital and phygital channels.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Utmost good faith' affects distribution because:
o: It applies only to the insurer
It permits agents to fill forms on the customer's behalf without verification
The distributor must ensure the proposer discloses all material facts, since non-disclosure can void the policy and lead to claim repudiation
e: The agent's duty under the code of conduct includes explaining the need for full disclosure; inadequate disclosure at sale is a leading cause of claim disputes.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Group insurance distribution differs from individual distribution mainly because:
o: Group policies are sold only online
Group policies cannot be sold by brokers
The buying decision is made by an employer or affinity group on behalf of members, so selling is B2B and relationship-based
e: Group business is sold to institutions through relationship managers and brokers, with negotiated terms, rather than to individual members.

topic: Intermediaries
t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: Which metric most directly measures customer retention for a general insurer?
o: Renewal retention ratio (policies renewed ÷ policies due for renewal)
e: The renewal ratio captures how many existing customers stay; it is the general-insurance counterpart of life insurance persistency.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: A life insurer had 10,000 policies issued in a month; 13 months later, 7,600 were in force and 2,400 had lapsed. The 13th-month persistency by count is:
e: 7,600 ÷ 10,000 = 76%. Persistency by premium may differ if lapsed policies had larger or smaller premiums than average.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: A 'single view of the customer' in CRM means:
o: The customer can see only one product
Only one agent may contact a customer
All of a customer's policies, interactions and complaints across channels are consolidated in one record
Each channel keeps its own separate customer file
e: A unified customer record enables consistent service and cross-sell across agents, branches, call centres and digital channels — the essence of collaborative CRM.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: Which of the following is a 'moment of truth' with the highest impact on loyalty in insurance?
o: The colour of the policy folder
e: Claims are when the promise is tested; a smooth, empathetic claim process creates advocates, while a poor one drives churn and negative word of mouth.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: 'Customer advocacy' in the loyalty ladder means the customer:
o: Actively recommends the insurer or agent to others
e: Advocates are at the top of the loyalty ladder; referrals from them are the lowest-cost source of new business for agents.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: 'Suitability' assessment before recommending a product means ensuring that:
o: The product is the insurer's newest launch
The product matches the customer's needs, financial capacity, risk profile and time horizon
The product gives the agent the highest commission
The product has the lowest premium
e: Suitability is the core of conduct-of-business best practice; documenting it protects both the customer and the insurer against mis-selling complaints.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Which of the following is a best practice in training of distributors?
o: Training only on the highest-commission product
Continuous training covering products, regulations, soft skills and digital tools, with periodic assessment
No training for corporate agents' staff
e: Ongoing training raises productivity and compliance; IRDAI also prescribes training/examination requirements for Specified Persons, ISPs and POSPs.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: 'Mystery shopping' is used by insurers mainly to:
o: Audit the actual sales conduct of distributors by posing as prospective customers
e: Mystery shopping checks whether distributors follow the sales process, disclose correctly and avoid misrepresentation, and feeds into coaching and disciplinary action.

topic: Reinsurance
t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The obligatory cession was reduced to 4% from 1 April 2022.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: A customer complains that his agent promised 'guaranteed 12% returns' on a participating endowment plan. The agent's statement is:
o: A misrepresentation prohibited by the code of conduct, since bonuses are not guaranteed
Correct because endowment plans always give 12%
Allowed if the customer signs the proposal
e: Agents must not make unrealistic promises or guarantee non-guaranteed benefits; benefit illustrations at prescribed rates exist precisely to prevent this.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Which performance indicator best reflects QUALITY (rather than volume) of an agent's business?
e: Persistency shows whether the policies sold were suitable and well explained; volume metrics alone can mask mis-selling.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: Bima Sugam has been set up under IRDAI regulations as a:
o: Not-for-profit company (Section 8) in which insurers hold shares
e: The IRDAI (Bima Sugam – Insurance Electronic Marketplace) Regulations, 2024 provide for a Section 8 not-for-profit company owned by life, general and health insurers.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: Which of the following is an example of an innovation tested under the Regulatory Sandbox?
o: Usage-based motor insurance ('pay as you drive')
e: Sandbox proposals have included usage-based, blockchain-enabled, cyber and other innovative products, processes and distribution methods.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: IRDAI's reforms in 2022–23 moved from a 'rule-based' to a 'principle-based' regulatory approach. One consequence for distribution was:
o: Introduction of fixed commission rates for each product
Removal of product-wise commission caps in favour of a board-approved commission policy within EoM limits
e: Principle-based regulation gives insurers flexibility (e.g. in commission, product launch via Use and File) while holding boards accountable for outcomes.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: A corporate agent (bank) tied with three life insurers before 2022 wishes to add more partners. Under current regulations it may add up to:
o: Six more, for a total of nine life insurers
Three more, for a total of six
e: The 2022 amendment allows nine insurers per category; a bank with three life tie-ups may therefore add six more life insurers.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: The 'Insurance Ombudsman' can entertain complaints where the value of the claim including expenses is up to:
e: The Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended in 2021) set the limit at ₹50 lakh; the ombudsman can also hear complaints against agents, brokers and other intermediaries.
